findings.text: Roundtrip through bitmap_to_arr32 then bitmap_from_arr32 preserves the requested prefix exactly while clearing leftover tail bits up to machine word rounding and leaving the following guard word untouched.

Roundtrip through bitmap_to_arr64 then bitmap_from_arr64 preserves the requested prefix, masks off unused high bits in the final partial element, clears bitmap tail bits beyond the length, and preserves the guard element after the prefix.

Range updates with bitmap_set and __bitmap_set agree across misaligned starts and lengths, range clears with bitmap_clear and __bitmap_clear agree likewise, and predicates bitmap_equal and __bitmap_equal agree on all compared outcomes.

Traversal with for_each_set_clump8 visits only eight bit groups containing set bits and reports each group start with its byte value, covering singletons, boundary spanning runs, repeated values, full bytes and discontiguous bits.

Enumeration with for_each_set_bit visits every set position once in increasing order, for_each_set_bit_from visits only positions at or after its start, and for_each_set_bit_wrap cycles from an arbitrary start through the end then from zero to cover every set position once.
Enumeration with for_each_clear_bit visits every clear position once, while for_each_clear_bit_from treats positions before its start as already visited and reproduces only the suffix.
Enumeration with for_each_set_bitrange and for_each_clear_bitrange coalesces maximal contiguous runs into start and end pairs, and the from variants suppress any portion before the start offset.

Counts from bitmap_weight and bitmap_weight_from are additive over complementary splits, a suffix starting beyond the length yields an empty result, and padding bits beyond the length in the final word do not contribute.

Operation bitmap_cut excises a slice at a start with a length and compacts higher bits downward, handling empty cuts, sub word and word aligned cases, single and multi word spans, and lengths beyond exact word multiples.
Use of bitmap_cut must remain correct when source and destination overlap by one word, requiring ordered accesses that do not clobber unread input.

Rendering with bitmap_print_bitmask_to_buf uses comma separated hexadecimal groups with trailing newline, bitmap_print_list_to_buf uses comma separated indices and dash ranges with trailing newline, both report full logical length including terminator, and list rendering supports resuming at a byte offset for outputs exceeding a page.
A cut test vector holds unsigned positions named first and cut with total length named nbits, plus a four element input word collection and a four element expected word collection.
A print test vector holds a constant word pointer named bitmap with length named nbits and two constant character pointers named mask and list for expected renderings.

Small single word manipulations involving bitmap_clear with bitmap_set, __change_bit with bitmap_shift_right, bitmap_complement with __assign_bit, plus queries bitmap_weight and bitmap_full and test_bit, are required to fold to compile time constants.

Use of bitmap_write for one bit affects only the addressed position, zero length writes leave the bitmap unchanged, and multi bit writes up to machine word width followed by bitmap_read preserve neighbours and return the written value at every offset.
Test width TEST_BIT_LEN equals 1000.

Import and export between bitmaps and word arrays must clear tail bits beyond the requested length both inside the final partial word and up to rounded word boundary, preventing stale bits from appearing as set.
